newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP rapporteur demands more protection for children.
newsitem.headline: EP rapporteur demands more protection for children.

text.p: The only healthy society is one that puts the needs of its smallest, most vulnerable, most inarticulate members first, the author of a European Parliament report on adoption said on Wednesday.
"Children's rights should actually take priority over adults' rights," Italian Christian Democrat Carlos Casini told the European Union assembly.

"Society should help the weak more than it helps the strong," Casini insisted, echoing the words of Wilmya Zimmermann, the author of a separate Parliament report which calls for more action to protect children from sexual abuse, violence, abandonment and destitution.
"No-one should be able to maintain that it doesn't matter for tomorrow's society how we treat our children," Anita Gradin, the EU's justice and home affairs commissioner, told Euro-MPs.
"Today's children are tomorrow's adults," she said.
In the case of adoption, putting children first meant focusing on children's right to a family, rather than on childless couples' right to adopt a child, Casini said.
The fall in birth rates in Europe meant there were 10 requests for adoption for each abandoned child, he explained.
This situation had led to a boom in cross-border adoption from countries like Romania which was not always above board and did not always put children's well-being first, he said.
The Italian Euro-MP argued it was better for children to stay with their natural families if possible, even if that meant providing assistance. Adoption should only be for orphans.
Gradin agreed: "Children have the right...first of all to a biological family. Only when that is not possible is it in the interests of the child to use adoption."

On Thursday, the Parliament is expected to approve a report in which Casini urges the EU member states to improve their adoption procedures, including only dealing with recognised organisations, especially in the case of cross-border adoption.
Swedish commissioner Gradin said she supported Casini in wanting all the EU countries to ratify the 1993 Hague Convention which provides a clear legal framework for adoption.
Gradin said it was also vital to make sure people could not go back on the decision to adopt a child.
"The adopted child should have exactly the same security as a biological child. It should never be possible for adoptive parents to decide to give back the adopted child," she said.
"Adults can divorce but parents should never be able to divorce a child."
